name: PLFM_RADAR
description: Open-source, low-cost 10.5 GHz PLFM phased array RADAR system
one_liner: Blueprints and firmware to build your own low-cost radar system that can detect and track objects like drones, out of off-the-shelf electronics.
buyer: A drone-detection or small-defense-tech hardware startup that needs a cheap radar reference design instead of designing phased array hardware from scratch.
business_use_cases: A drone-defense startup uses the open hardware design as a starting point to build and sell low-cost counter-drone detection units to airports or stadiums.
A university robotics lab builds a few units to give students hands-on radar/beamforming experience instead of buying commercial lab equipment.
A hobbyist electronics kit company sells assembled or partial kits of the AERIS-10N (short-range version) to makers and SDR enthusiasts.

money_ideas.idea: Sell assembled or DIY hardware kits of the 3km-range version to makers, students, and drone hobbyists.
Offer paid design consulting to startups adapting this reference design into a commercial product.

steal_this: This is a hardware R&D project, not a weekend product — the realistic move is sourcing the BOM and building one demo unit to show at a maker faire or pitch to a drone-security startup as a paid customization job, not shipping anything productized this weekend.
